statement.text:
Let G be a residually finite 2-group and let x ∈ G be a left 3-Engel element
of order 2. Is ⟨xG ⟩ locally nilpotent?
    It is known that in any group a 3-Engel element of odd order belongs to the
locally nilpotent radical (E. Jabara, G. Traustason, Proc. Amer. Math. Soc., 147,
no. 5 (2019), 1921–1927).
    Comment of 2025: An element a ∈ G is called a strong left 3-Engel element if
⟨a, ag ⟩ is nilpotent of class at most 2 and ⟨a, ag , ah ⟩ is nilpotent of class at most 3 for
all g, h ∈ G. (This is equivalent to a being left 3-Engel when a is of odd order.) It is
proved that if a is a strong left 3-Engel element in an arbitrary group G, then ⟨a⟩G is
locally nilpotent (A. Hadjievangelou, G. Traustason, Proc. Amer. Math. Soc., 152,
no. 4 (2024), 1467–1477).                                                       G. Traustason
